job.title: Occupational Health & Safety Advisor
job.description:
ABOUT THEM
This large and highly regarded healthcare organisation provides essential services across a diverse network of sites throughout Melbourne’s south-east.
With a complex workforce spanning clinical and non-clinical environments, health and safety is a key organisational priority. 

ABOUT THE ROLE
Reporting to the OHS Manager, you will provide specialist health and safety advice and support within a large and complex healthcare environment. The role has a strong stakeholder focus, partnering with leaders, managers, Health and Safety Representatives and employees to build capability and support positive safety outcomes.
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Facilitate incident investigations, hazard identification and risk assessments, identifying root causes and appropriate controls to prevent recurrence.
  • Coach and support managers and HSRs to strengthen local OHS practices and build safety capability.
  • Provide specialist advice on OHS legislation, regulatory obligations and the practical management of workplace health and safety risks.
  • Conduct workplace audits and inspections and work with stakeholders to address identified risks and areas of non-compliance.
  • Support effective consultation through Health and Safety Committees, HSRs and other stakeholder forums.
  • Contribute to OHS projects, working groups and broader health and safety initiatives.
ABOUT YOU
You will be an experienced Health and Safety professional who enjoys being visible within the business, building relationships and working closely with operational stakeholders. You will bring a practical and solutions-focused approach, with the confidence to coach and influence across a diverse and complex environment.
You will ideally bring:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Occupational Health and Safety or a related discipline or a Certificate IV in WHS
  • Experience in an OHS Advisor, Health & Safety Advisor or similar role.
  • Sound knowledge of Victorian OHS legislation and regulatory requirements.
  • Experience working with HSRs and formal consultation structures.
Experience within healthcare, public sector or another large and complex operational environment will be highly regarded.

APPLY
Please apply via the link or contact Becka at bbrown@thesafestep.com.au for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Head of Work Health and Safety
job.description:
Join one of Victoria's largest and fastest-growing councils and play a pivotal role in creating a safer, healthier and more resilient workplace. Serving a diverse community of more than 400,000 residents and over 36,000 businesses, the City of Casey offers the opportunity to lead enterprise-wide Health, Safety & Wellbeing strategy while driving meaningful cultural change and capability uplift.

Based at our award-winning Bunjil Place headquarters, you will partner with leaders across the organisation to embed physical and psychological safety into everyday decision-making and deliver lasting benefits for our people, organisation and community.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Chief People Officer, you will provide enterprise-wide leadership across health, safety, wellbeing, injury management and workers compensation. You'll lead the continued uplift of governance, risk management, psychosocial safety and leadership accountability while establishing a high-performing Health, Safety & Wellbeing Centre of Excellence.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading the delivery of Health, Safety & Wellbeing strategy.
  • Strengthening safety governance, assurance and compliance frameworks.
  • Driving a proactive approach to critical risk management and psychosocial safety.
  • Enhancing injury management, return-to-work and workers compensation performance.
  • Building leadership capability and embedding a strong, learning-focused safety culture.
  • Using data and insights to improve safety outcomes and organisational resilience.
About You

You are an accomplished safety leader who combines strategic thinking with operational excellence. You have demonstrated experience leading health, safety and wellbeing functions in complex organisations and can influence leaders at all levels to drive accountability and meaningful change.
You will bring:
  • Expertise across WHS governance, risk management, psychosocial safety and injury management.
  • A track record of building safety culture and improving organisational risk maturity.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and leadership capability.
  • The credibility, courage and judgement to lead complex conversations and deliver sustainable outcomes.

job.title: Manager HSE Systems and Assurance
job.description:
An opportunity for a senior Health & Safety leader to take a key role across safety systems, compliance and assurance supporting operations across multiple Australian states.
  
This role will provide leadership across the organisation’s safety management system and assurance agenda, while continuing to provide practical, expert safety advice and support across the business.
  
This is a broad, multi-state role requiring someone who can operate strategically while remaining close to operations - working with leaders, employees, contractors and regulators to strengthen systems, lift capability and drive continuous improvement.
  
The role
You will:
  • Lead and continuously improve health and safety standards, systems, tools and processes
  • Provide specialist advice across safety legislation, risk, systems and regulatory requirements
  • Lead the regulatory compliance framework across safety and broader technical obligations
  • Oversee assurance and audit programs, including the effectiveness of critical risk controls and management systems  
What you will bring
We are looking for an experienced safety professional with strong technical depth, commercial judgement and the ability to influence.

You will bring:
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Health & Safety, Health Sciences, Engineering or a related disciplines
  • Leadership experience and influencing across broad stakeholder groups
  • Demonstrated experience implementing and maintaining safety management systems, standards and procedures
  • Strong assurance and audit capability, including developing programs and translating findings into measurable improvement  
Your approach
  • You will be someone who builds strong relationships while maintaining independent professional judgement
  • You are practical, resilient and comfortable working through complexity, with the ability to see the connection between operational risk, management systems, regulatory obligations and business performance
  • You will be equally comfortable providing strategic advice, challenging thinking, coaching leaders and getting into the detail when required.

job.title: Site EHS Manager

Why This Role?

This is an outstanding opportunity for a proven operational safety professional who wants broader exposure and leadership responsibility without losing touch with the workforce. You'll join a collaborative national safety team, gain exposure to senior stakeholders, and play a key role in shaping site culture while building the experience needed for future leadership opportunities. The business offers a supportive, down-to-earth environment where relationships, trust and visible leadership are highly valued.

job.title: Head of HSE Operations
job.description:
HEAD OF HSEQ OPERATIONS

National Executive Safety Leadership Opportunity (based in Brisbane/Sydney or Melbourne)

ABOUT THE COMPANY

An established and nationally recognised Australian transport organisation is seeking an experienced safety leader to join its senior leadership team.
Operating across multiple jurisdictions, the organisation delivers essential public services through a geographically dispersed workforce and complex, high-risk operational environments. Safety is fundamental to its success, and the business has established a strong safety culture and industry-leading safety outcomes relative to its peer group.

Continued growth, the integration of new operations and increasing complexity across the risk landscape have created an opportunity for a senior safety professional to influence safety performance at a national level.
This is also an organisation that invests in its people, with genuine succession pathways and opportunities for high-performing leaders to progress into broader executive roles.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting directly to the General Manager HSEQ, the Head of HSEQ Operations is a pivotal national leadership position responsible for driving consistency, capability, governance and continual improvement across the organisation.

This is not a desk-bound corporate safety role. The successful candidate will combine strategic thinking with strong operational credibility, working closely with Managing Directors, operational leaders and regional safety teams to identify emerging risks and deliver practical improvements.
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Analyse safety data, trends and leading indicators to identify emerging and high-consequence risks.
  • Develop and implement national safety improvement initiatives.
  • Strengthen consistency across safety systems, processes and standards.
  • Lead and support major incident and ICAM investigations, ensuring organisational learning is embedded.
  • Provide assurance across integrated management systems, ISO frameworks, compliance and audit programs.
  • Consolidate and interpret national safety data to provide meaningful insight to Executive and Board stakeholders.
  • Mentor and develop regional safety leaders and build safety capability across the organisation.
  • Partner with operational leaders to deliver sustainable improvements while balancing governance with commercial and operational realities.
The role has significant national influence, including a dotted-line leadership relationship with regional safety professionals across multiple operating divisions.

ABOUT YOU

You will be an experienced safety leader who is comfortable operating in complex, high-risk and geographically dispersed environments.
You are likely to bring:
  • Significant senior HSEQ leadership experience across transport, rail, logistics, infrastructure, construction, mining, manufacturing or another comparable high-risk industry.
  • Strong operational risk management capability, ideally including heavy vehicle or transport-related risk.
  • Experience with ISO-certified management systems, audit and assurance.
  • Proven ICAM and serious incident investigation capability.
  • Experience working across multiple sites, jurisdictions and diverse operational cultures.
  • Strong analytical capability, with the ability to turn safety data into meaningful business insight.
  • The credibility to influence senior executives while remaining connected to frontline operations.
Most importantly, you will be a practical, collaborative and emotionally mature leader who builds relationships before implementing change.
You will be confident challenging constructively, comfortable operating under pressure and capable of influencing without relying on authority. You will understand that effective safety leadership is ultimately about earning trust, building capability and helping operational leaders achieve better outcomes.
This is an exceptional opportunity for a senior safety professional who wants to move beyond functional leadership and make a genuine national impact, while positioning themselves for future broader executive leadership opportunities.

job.title: Senior Psychosocial Risk & Wellbeing Manager
job.description:
A leading and highly respected Australian institution is seeking an experienced Senior (Psychosocial) Health & Wellbeing Manager to play a pivotal role in shaping and embedding a contemporary psychosocial risk management and psychological health strategy across a complex, large scale environment.

This is a unique opportunity for a senior practitioner who combines strategic thinking with practical execution and is passionate about creating psychologically safe, healthy and high performing workplaces.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Head of Health & Wellbeing, this position will lead the implementation and ongoing evolution of an enterprise Health & Wellbeing Framework, with an immediate focus on psychosocial risk management, psychological health and psychological injury prevention.
Significant foundational work has already been completed, including frameworks, tools, risk assessment methodologies and supporting resources. The challenge now is to bring these components together into a cohesive operating model, drive organisation wide adoption and deliver measurable outcomes.
This is not a traditional wellbeing role. It is a strategic leadership opportunity focused on embedding mature psychosocial risk practices across a large and complex organisation.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead implementation and continuous improvement of the Health & Wellbeing Framework.
  • Drive a proactive psychosocial risk management program across the organisation.
  • Develop consistent approaches to triage, risk assessment, controls and case management.
  • Analyse organisational data to identify trends, emerging risks and intervention opportunities.
  • Influence and partner with senior leaders and specialist functions to deliver coordinated responses to complex psychosocial matters.
  • Strengthen organisational capability through coaching, education and stakeholder engagement.
  • Provide expert advice on psychological health, psychosocial risk and injury prevention.
  • Support the development of governance, reporting and assurance processes that drive accountability and continuous improvement.
About You
We are interested in experienced professionals who have successfully led organisational change and implemented psychosocial risk, wellbeing or psychological health frameworks within complex environments.
You will bring:
  • Deep expertise in psychosocial risk management, workplace psychological health or organisational wellbeing.
  • Demonstrated success implementing strategic programs across large, multi stakeholder organisations.
  • Strong influencing and relationship building capability.
  • The ability to navigate complexity, ambiguity and competing priorities.
  • A pragmatic and outcomes focused approach that balances strategy with execution.
  • Experience using data and insights to shape interventions and measure impact.
While qualifications in Organisational Psychology, Occupational Health, Health & Safety or a related discipline would be highly regarded, demonstrated experience and achievement in delivering similar outcomes will be most important.
Candidates from corporate, government, healthcare, infrastructure, education, professional services or other complex environments are encouraged to apply.

Why This Role?
This is an opportunity to join a collaborative and high performing team where strong stakeholder relationships already exist and there is genuine executive commitment to improving psychosocial health outcomes.
You will have the opportunity to:
  • Influence organisation wide strategy and culture.
  • Lead a critical and highly visible agenda.
  • Partner with senior leaders across a diverse and complex environment.
  • Build sustainable systems that improve psychological health and wellbeing outcomes at scale.
  • Make a meaningful contribution to the health, safety and wellbeing of thousands of people.
Package & Flexibility
  • Hybrid working model
  • Sydney based
  • Exceptional opportunity to shape and influence a growing psychosocial risk and wellbeing function
For a confidential discussion, please contact Stephen Coldicutt at The Safe Step or apply via SEEK.

job.title: Health & Safety Advisor - Esperance

job.title: Health and Safety Business Partner
job.description:

You will work as an embedded member of the brand leadership team, partnering with General Managers to drive improved safety performance, strengthen leadership capability and deliver practical improvements across a large national store network.

While initially aligned to one brand, this role operates with a broader Group mindset and has enterprise level connections. You will have the opportunity to collaborate with Health and Safety Business Partners across other brands and contribute to Group wide initiatives, projects and improvements.

This is not a traditional safety advisor role. You will not be expected to do safety for the business. Instead, you will provide the advice, coaching, challenge and practical tools that enable operational leaders to own and deliver safety.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Partner with senior leaders to drive proactive safety outcomes
  • Provide trusted advice and practical support across operational teams
  • Translate safety strategy into practical, operational actions
  • Coach leaders to build safety capability, ownership and accountability
  • Challenge and influence leaders to strengthen safety performance and culture
  • Conduct store visits and partner with Regional and Area Managers
  • Identify risks, trends and opportunities for improvement
  • Build leadership capability through coaching and mentoring
Position Skills and Qualifications:
  • Formal qualifications in Health and Safety, WHS, OHS or similar
  • 5+ years' Health and Safety experience, ideally in a Business Partner or senior advisory role
  • Experience in complex, multi site or geographically dispersed operations
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and ability to influence senior leaders
  • Proven ability to coach, challenge and build leadership capability
  • Strong knowledge of safety culture and risk management
  • Confident, credible and comfortable respectfully pushing back when required
  • Autonomous, practical and commercially minded
  • Experience in retail or a similar large operational environment with large volumes of geographically dispersed sites is desirable
The Ideal Person:
You will be an experienced and credible safety professional who can comfortably move between the store floor and the senior leadership table.
You will have the confidence and experience to hold your own in robust conversations, challenge thinking when required and provide practical recommendations that leaders can understand and implement.

Importantly, you will enjoy coaching others rather than doing the work for them. You will understand how to build safety capability through operational leaders and know how to influence outcomes across a large and geographically dispersed business.

Join the Team:
This is an excellent opportunity to take on a genuine Health & Safety Business Partner role where you will have the autonomy, trust and visibility to make a real impact.

With a strong focus on lifting capability, strengthening consistency and supporting leaders to take ownership of safety, this role will suit someone who enjoys being operationally connected while also having a genuine seat at the table.

job.title: Director, Safety I VicGrid
job.description:
Join VicGrid and help shape the safety culture behind Victoria's next generation of energy infrastructure.

Location options: Melbourne or Regional Victoria

The Safe Step is proud to be partnering with VicGrid in seeking an accomplished Director, Safety to provide strategic and operational health and safety leadership across its Renewable Energy Zone (REZ) developments and broader portfolio of major energy infrastructure projects.

About VicGrid
VicGrid is a Victorian State Business Corporation responsible for planning Victoria’s transmission network and Renewable Energy Zones as the state transitions towards renewable energy. VicGrid is taking a coordinated approach to developing the transmission infrastructure Victoria needs to maintain a reliable and affordable electricity supply as ageing coal-fired generation retires.

The scale and complexity of VicGrid’s work is substantial.  Its current portfolio of projects will play an important role in reshaping Victoria's energy network and represent some of the state's most significant current and future infrastructure investment.

About the Opportunity
As Director, Safety and a member of the VicGrid Leadership Team, you will lead VicGrid's health and safety function and develop a high-performing Safety team, supporting the safe development and delivery of its programs. You will play a critical role in embedding safety into project planning and delivery while driving a positive, proactive and industry-leading safety culture.

You will lead the implementation of VicGrid's safety strategy, project risk and assurance activities and contractor safety frameworks, while providing trusted advice to Program Directors and senior leaders across the organisation.

Working across a complex stakeholder environment, you will have the opportunity to shape safety standards, behaviours and practices across VicGrid's project portfolio and the broader industry.

About you
You will be a highly experienced safety leader with a strong track record working across major infrastructure/construction, energy, utilities or similarly complex project environments.

You will combine deep technical safety expertise with the leadership presence and influencing capability required to operate effectively with executives, senior project leaders, contractors, regulators and government stakeholders.

Experience working within an active client model, with the ability to effectively influence delivery partners, provide appropriate governance and assurance, and navigate the balance between oversight and contractor accountability, is highly regarded.

You will bring:
  • A credible and pragmatic safety leadership approach, with strong executive presence balanced with humility, curiosity and authenticity.
  • The ability to connect with diverse teams and stakeholders, harness existing capability and bring people with you.
  • High levels of judgement, with the ability to prioritise and move comfortably between hands-on delivery, strategic thinking and senior-level influence.
  • Experience driving cultural change through safety initiatives and programs.
  • Strong leadership capability, with demonstrated experience developing high-performing teams.
  • The ability to provide strategic advice and constructive challenge at executive and senior project leadership level.
  • Strong project and risk management capability within complex, high-profile delivery environments.
  • The ability to lead and navigate significant organisational and industry change.
Why join VicGrid?
The 2025 Victorian Transmission Plan sets out a long-term, coordinated approach to the development of Victoria's energy infrastructure network. As VicGrid continues to lead planning, coordination and delivery across a significant portfolio of energy infrastructure initiatives, this role offers a unique opportunity to influence how major projects are safely developed and delivered across the state.

As Director, Safety, you will provide strategic leadership during a pivotal period for Victoria's energy transition, embedding a safety-first culture and establishing the frameworks, governance and capability that will support the successful delivery of VicGrid's objectives for years to come.
